AI project handover: what the delivery team owes you

A vendor hands over a repository on Friday. On Monday, your engineer discovers that a scheduled job still uses the vendor’s account. Before the engagement ends, have the people who will operate the application complete a change using only company-owned access.

Build a handover register

Create one row for each repository, build pipeline, runtime, database, model account and scheduled job. Record the business owner, technical owner, billing account, recovery contact and location of the access procedure. Store credential references in the register. Keep the actual secrets in your secret manager.

Rehearse the first independent release

Ask a company engineer to change one staging setting, deploy the reviewed revision and locate its release identifier. The vendor observes and notes where the runbook fails. Repeat the exercise with a different operator after fixing the instructions. A successful vendor-led screen share does not show whether either operator can do the work alone.

Recover data as well as software

Use an isolated database for the rehearsal. Restore a recent backup and verify a known business record plus its attachments. Then ask the operator to trace a single failed request from its public identifier into the relevant logs. Keep the measured time and the missing permissions with the acceptance record.

Decision table
Handover itemProof to retain
Source and releaseCommit, build record, deploying identity and working rollback procedure.
Production dependenciesInventory of external APIs, quotas, billing owners and renewal dates.
Data recoveryRestore timestamp, record checked and person who performed it.
Vendor exitRevoked test identity and a successful subsequent run under a company account.

Make the decision

Tie final acceptance to the exercises that matter for this application. A successful deployment cannot compensate for an untested restore. Assign any outstanding recovery or monitoring task to a named person with a deadline and agree who supports incidents in the meantime.
